quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
To turn off the seat belt buzzer or light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They become better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: To turn safely, turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
All passengers must use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under should ride in the back seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a car with an airbag.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Follow closely behind the vehicle ahead of you.
Keep a two-second distance behind the vehicle ahead of you.
Pull over on the right side of the road and stop.

questions.explanation: For safety, slow down and stay alert in work zones. Keep a 4-second distance behind other vehicles, avoid changing lanes, and be patient around workers.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your freeway exit?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop, back up, or swerve across lanes on the highway. Do not cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What documents must a driver show if stopped for a violation?
questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must have all three documents in your vehicle when driving.

questions.question: When should you check your blind spot over your shoulder?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol?

options.text: They always know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that harms judgment, vision, focus, understanding of reality, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway is starting. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves right and you should slow down to 35 mph.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:

options.text: Make the effects of both weaker.
Make the effects of both stronger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make the effects of both stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs makes both effects stronger. It is unsafe to drive after alcohol or drugs alone, and even more dangerous to mix them.

questions.question: Driving ability can be harmed by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness all harm your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When you see an angry driver near you, you should:
questions.explanation: When another driver is angry, stay away from them. Do not make eye contact or use gestures that could make them angrier. Slow down or move away to keep yourself safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you need to change how you drive.
You should slow down in rain and fog.
Watch for cars coming up behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Change your driving when weather changes suddenly. Always slow down in rain and fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: If you see a horse and rider on the road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn them.
Drive next to the horse so it gets used to cars.
Speed up to pass the horse quickly.

questions.explanation: Always drive slowly near animals to avoid frightening them. Do not honk, speed up, or drive too close. Horses can be unpredictable and may run into your path if scared.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when you see:

options.text: A traffic officer signaling you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and when a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: You should signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving the curb because:

options.text: It is only needed if other cars are nearby.
It is a good habit and the law requires it.
It is only needed during the move, not before.
It is not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. The law requires this. Always signal before leaving the curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.explanation: At night, you can see less. Use your headlights and drive slow enough to stop within the distance you can see.
